title: Revenue Cycle Standard: Charge Credits and Duplicate Test Charges on Laboratory Test Orders
content:
## The credit line

Each credit line on a Laboratory Test Orders order points to exactly one charge line or add-on line of the same order and credits that line's full amount. Partial credits do not exist. A charge line may be credited at most once: a line that already has a credit pointing to it is not credited again.

## Credit reasons

The credit reasons are fixed:

| Credit reason | Used for |
|---|---|
| Cancelled before testing | A patient cancellation |
| Test not performed | Hold expiry, requisition expiry, or a test declined with ABN option 3 |
| Specimen rejected, not recollected | A rejection with no recollection, or a lapsed recollection window |
| Duplicate test | A duplicate charge, as defined below |
| Billing correction | A line posted at a price other than its test-menu list price; it is credited and re-posted at the correct price |

## Duplicate charges

A charge is a duplicate when the same patient has the same test charged, and not credited, on another order that is not cancelled. That other order's collection date must fall within the class's duplicate-test window, in calendar days, counted back from this order's collection date (the collection date being day 0). The later-collected line is the one credited. A class whose duplicate-test window is 0 never treats a repeat as a duplicate.

**Example (hypothetical, a class with a 7-day window).** A test is collected on 2 June on one order and again on 5 June on another order of the same patient. Neither order is cancelled and neither line is credited. The 5 June line has a same-test charge collected 3 days earlier, so it is the duplicate and is credited with the reason *duplicate test*; the 2 June line stands.

**Example (hypothetical, a billing correction).** A line posted at 50.00 for a test whose menu list price is 48.00 is credited in full (50.00) and re-posted at 48.00.
